Name: Python (python.org installer)
Description: The python.org installer, wrapped with the two properties that decide whether a fleet deployment is visible at all.
Awkwardness: The python.org installer defaults to a per-user install under the user's AppData. Intune runs it as SYSTEM, so the default lands Python in the SYSTEM profile, where the deployment reports success and not one user can find python on their machine. InstallAllUsers=1 is the difference, and PrependPath=1 only touches the machine PATH when it is set alongside. The second trap is versioning: 3.12 and 3.13 install side by side rather than upgrading, so a wrapper whose version marches from 3.12 to 3.13 describes an upgrade that did not happen - the old interpreter is still there, still on PATH depending on order, and still what some scripts pick up.
SetupFileHint: python-X.Y.Z-amd64.exe (the full installer, not the web or embeddable build).
Notes: NOT tested in this repository. The properties are transcribed from the python.org installer documentation and have not been run here.
InstallAllUsers=1 is the one that matters. Without it, an Intune deployment installs into the SYSTEM profile and looks successful.
PrependPath=1 only affects the machine PATH when InstallAllUsers=1 is also set. On its own it edits the SYSTEM account's PATH, which helps nobody.
Include_test=0 omits the test suite; drop it if you actually want it.

Uninstall runs the same installer with /uninstall /quiet, which is why the payload stays in the install folder rather than being deleted after the install. That is documented behaviour but, like the rest of this recipe, untested here.
A minor-version bump is a side-by-side install, not an upgrade. If you want only one interpreter on a device, uninstall the previous package rather than relying on this one to supersede it.
Set Version to the Python version you downloaded.

Arp.Comments: The python.org installer wrapped as an MSI, forced per-machine. Properties from vendor documentation, untested.
